checks.reason: The deliberately vulnerable Supabase source fixture grants private-note reads to both ordinary and anonymous callers. This is source evidence only.

findings.title: Unconditional policy permits reads of owner-only notes
findings.impact: Given the fixture’s declared private-note model, the SELECT grant and unconditional RLS policy would expose those records to anon and authenticated roles if deployed as shown. No deployment was inspected.
reproduction: Inspect the alternative vulnerable SQL fixture and its SELECT grants.
Compare the public_read policy with the owner_read policy in the secure counterpart.
Proposed runtime test, not executed against Supabase: seed a synthetic note, verify its owner can read it, and assert an unrelated user and anonymous caller cannot.
evidence: vulnerable.sql grants SELECT to anon and authenticated and uses a true SELECT predicate.
The Flutter and React Native source snippets query the same conceptual notes endpoint; client filters cannot replace the database policy.
findings.remediation: For the declared owner-only model, restrict SELECT to the owner identity as illustrated by the secure counterpart; review all other applicable policies and grants.
findings.retest: Run ordinary-user and anonymous access tests in an isolated Supabase project, including a successful owner baseline. Not executed in this source review.
